JUDGMENT The Petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 against respondents, for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. Brief facts of the petitioner's case are that, on 20.04.2022 at about 11.30 p.m. the petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41/H-4902 on Old Madras Road from NGEF towards K.R.
Puram, Opposite Gopalan Mall, wherein the driver of Bolero Maxi Truck bearing Reg.No.KA-51/B-9206 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, at high speed came from same direction and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident he was shifted to K.R. Puram Government Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and further shifted to NIMHANS and again Janapriya Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and treated in ICU.

During hospitalization X-rays and CT Scan were taken which revealed that the petitioner had sustained traumatic brain injury, left temporoparietal EDH s/p left temporoparietal craniotomy and evacuation of EDH and left clavicle fracture and other injuries.

Thereafter shifted to NIMHANS Hospital wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 10.05.2022 to 31.05.2022 and on 24.04.2022 he underwent left emporoparietal craniotomy and evacuation of EDH and discharged on 31.05.2022 with an advice to regular follow up treatment and he has spent more than Rs.7,50,000/- towards medical expenses, food, transportation, conveyance and other charges.

The injury sustained by the petitioner are not healed and he is in coma, not able to take care of himself and not able to do his day to day activities and hence, a servant has been appointed to lookafter him by paying Rs.3,500/-p.m. and also home care nursing visited to home day by day for which he has spent huge amount.

2 4.

Prior to the accident the petitioner was hale, healthy, aged about 27 years and working as Chef at Leon Grill Hotel at Indiranagar and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. and he is only member in the family and due to the said accidental injuries he could not able to attend his job till today and lost salary and grief causing lot of pain, shock, mental agony and financial difficulties.

5. This accident occurred due to negligence of the driver of the Bolero Maxi Truck bearing Reg.No.KA-51/B-9206, hence, the Jeevan Bhimanagar Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of said vehicle in crime No.36/2022 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 to 3 are owner and insurers of the vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prayed to grant the compensation.
6. In pursuance to the notice, respondent No.1 and 3 have appeared through their respective counsel & filed their written statements.

Respondent No.2 did not appear before the Tribunal and hence he was placed exparte.
7.

Brief averments of the written statement of respondent No.1 is that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and he is the RC owner of Bolero Maxi Truck bearing Reg.No.KA-51/B-9206 and the said vehicle was insured with respondent No.3, the policy was in force as on the date of accident and the driver of the vehicle was having a valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
On the fault of the petitioner the accident had occurred and due to his negligence he has touched the back side of the vehicle.

Further, respondent No.1 has denied the name, address, age, income and occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by him and disability caused to him and also contended that, claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition with costs.

8. Brief averments of the written statement of respondent No.3 is that, there is 2 days delay in lodging the complaint and the alleged accident caused due to rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41/H-4902, the Bolero Maxi Truck not at all caused the accident.
As per the police complaint, FIR, panchanama it is mentioned that "unknown vehicle" dashed and it is self accident by the rider of the motorcycle himself.
As per the IMV report both the vehicles sustained damages on the front portion, as per the sketch, the place of accident shown on the middle of the road.
It is not forthcoming that when the alleged offending goods vehicle seized.
The IMV report prepared after 18 days from the date of accident.
The 133 notice issued to the respondent No.1 owner after 1 month from the date of accident, 19 days from the date of preparation of IMV report.

It is further contended that, the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle riding the same in a rash and negligent manner, without wearing helmet, without DL, without policy for motorcycle and met with self accident.
The Bolero Maxi Truck not at all dashed to the motorcycle, but to get compensation the petitioner files a false case against the driver of the Bolero Maxi Truck bearing Reg.No.KA-51/B-9206.

The petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties such as owner and insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41/H-4902 and also denied the issuance of insurance policy for the Bolero Maxi Truck vehicle.
It is further contended that the driver of the Bolero Maxi Truck was having valid and effective driving licence, FC, permit.

Further this respondent denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by him and disability caused to him and also contended that, claim of the petitioner is excessive and Gangadhar.M vs Syed Vahid on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161400527/
3 exorbitant.

9. On basis of the Pleadings and materials, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 20.04.2022 at about 11.30 p.m the petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41/H-4902 proceeding on Old Madras Road from NGRF towards K.R. Puram, when he reached near opposite Gopalan Mall at that time driver of one Bolero Maxi Truck bearing Reg.No.KA-51/B-9206, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering human life, came at high speed and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to forced impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous Injuries on vital parts of the body?
2)Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3) Whether order or award?
10.
In order to substantiate the case, petitioner got examined as PW.1 and got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to P.15.

The petitioner got examined the Medical Record Technician and Admin at NIMHANS Hospital as PW.2 and he got marked 02 documents at Ex.P.16 and P.17 and the petitioner examined another witness by name Sundar Murthy as PW.3, who is the Medical Record Officer of Janapriya Hospital and he got marked 2 documents at Ex.P.18 and P.19.

On the other hand, the respondent got examined the Doctor of K.R. Puram Hospital as RW.1 and he got marked a document at Ex.R.1 and got examined the Sub-Inspector of Ashok Nagar Police Statgion by name B.M. Harish Kumar as RW.2 and he got marked Ex.R.2 and R.3 and also got marked Ex.C.1 and C.2.
The respondent No.3 got examined its Legal Manager as RW.3 and he got marked 2 documents at Ex.R.4 and R.5.
11. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.

12. For the following reasons, this Tribunal answer the above Issues as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS 13. Issue No.1:-
The petitioner filed this petition against the respondents for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.

4 14. In order to substantiate his case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and filed his affidavit in lieu of chief examination.
In his chief examination affidavit, he had reiterated the entire averments of the petition and got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15.

Ex.P.1 is the copy of F.I.R. Ex.P.2 is the copy of complaint, Ex.P.3 is the copy of Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the copy of sketch, Ex.P.5 is the copy of IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the copy of Wound Certificate, Ex.P.7 is the notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act, Ex.P.8 is the reply of 133 notice, Ex.P.9 is the Charge Sheet, Ex.P.10 and 11 are the discharge summaries, Ex.P.12 is the referral letter, Ex.P.13 is the copy of Aadhar Card of the petitioner, Ex.P.14 is the medical bills and Ex.P.15 is the prescriptions.
In cross examination, he has stated that, after accident he was in Coma and don't know who lodged the complaint.
The Vehicle hit from back side and it was a Bolero.
The police traced the vehicle number through CC TV footage.
Further denied that, it is a self hit to the divider and got injured, the vehicle has been implicated.

15. The petitioner got examined the Medical Record Technician and Admin at NIMHANS Hospital as PW.2 and he got marked 02 documents at Ex.P.16 and P.17, which are the authorization letter and case sheets/inpatient records.
In cross examination, he has stated that, the patient is referred from other hospital, hence MLC would not be recorded.

16. The petitioner examined another witness by name Sundar Murthy as PW.3, who is the Medical Record Officer of Janapriya Hospital and he got marked 2 documents at Ex.P.18 and P.19, which are the authorization letter and inpatient records.
In cross examination, he has stated that, MLC is not recorded in this case as the patient came from K.R Puram Govt. hospital.
17. On the other hand, the respondent got examined the Doctor of K.R. Puram Hospital as RW.1 and she got marked a document at Ex.R.1 which is the MLC Extract.
R.W1 has stated that, She has given first Aid.
In Ex.R.1 after history, 'assault' is tampered and 'RTA' is over written, as by mistake it was mentioned as assault same sentence is continued by her as by Bolero, it is RTA only.
The witness treated as hostile by the counsel for Resp. No.3 and cross examined.
In cross examination she has stated that, the history was written in black ink, the black ink was over then she used blue ink.
She denied that, intentionally she inserted word RTA by scratching the word assault on the say of Police and patient.
Further stated that the patient was brought at mid-night 12.40 a.m. with bleeding and by mistake assault was written.

18. The respondent got examined the Sub-Inspector of Ashok Nagar Police Station by name B.M.
Harish Kumar as RW.2 and he got marked Ex.R.2 and R.3 and also got marked Ex.C.1 and C.2.
Ex.R.2 is the Police Intimation, Ex.R.3 is the MLC of Janapriya Hospital,
Ex.C.1 and C.2 are the letter issued by the RW.2 and vehicle movement letter.
He has stated that the accident took place on 20- 04-2022 and complaint was lodged on 22-04-2024.
He has completed the investigation and filed the charge sheet.
The witness treated hostile by the counsel for respondent No.3 and cross-examined.
In the cross- examination he has admitted that, in the complaint and FIR unknown vehicle is mentioned.
He visited the K.R. Puram Hospital on 21-04-2022 in between 2.00 a.m. to 3.00 a.m. and received the police intimation.
Further stated that in Ex.R.3, RTA is not mentioned but, met with an accident is mentioned.
As per his investigation, Bolero was hit from back side.
Further stated that, one Mahindra told that it was a goods vehicle for transportation of chicken live birds.
Further he denies that to help the petitioner he has falsely implicated the Borelo vehicle.

She has stated that,
there is 02 days delay in filing the complaint the vehicle number was not mentioned in the complaint.
The Bolero vehicle has been falsely implicated in this case.
In Ex.R.1 the word assault has been tampered and over written as RTA.
In the cross- examination she has admitted that, firstly the injured was taken to the K.R. Puram Govt. Hospital.
In Ex.P.19 the history was entered as accident took place by Bolero Vehicle.

20. The Counsel for the petitioner argued that, the 2 days delay in filing of the complaint has been properly explained as injured was in Coma, in Ex.P.19 the history is clearly mentioned as hit by bolero truck.
I.O. has secured the CC TV footage and collected the vehicle number.
Therefore, prays to award the compensation.

21. The Counsel for the Respondent No.3 argued that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the Petitioner himself and denied about the involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident.
Further argued that there is 2 days delay in filing the complaint, the complaint has been filed against unknown vehicle, Ex.R.1 is tampered.
Therefore, prays to dismiss the petition.
22. Respondent No.1 has contended that, there is a delay of two days in filing the complainant.
The MLC at Ex.R.1 has been tampered.
The offending vehicle is not involved in the case and it has been falsely implicated in this case.

On perusal of Ex.P.19 at page No.8, it appears that, the petitioner was admitted in the K.R. Puram General Hospital on 21-04-2022 at 12.44 a.m. and history is RTA as hit by Bolero near Gopalan Mall at 12.15 am on 21-04- 2022.
On perusal of page No.4, the petitioner was further admitted in Janapriya Hospitals and Health Care on 21- 04-2022 itself for further treatment and discharged on 24-04-2022.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.6 the would certificate issued by the Janapriya Hospitals, it appears that, the history is road traffic accident.

On perusal of these documents, it appears that, the petitioner was admitted in the K.R. Puram Govt. Hospital and Janapriya Hospital on 21/04/2022 for the injuries sustained in R.T.A and the medical records are entered on same day of the accident.
23.
On perusal of these documents, it appears that the petitioner was admitted in the hospital for the treatment and he was in Coma and his employer has filed the complaint.

On perusal of Ex.P.2, the first information, it appears that, filing of the information was delayed as injured was admitted in the hospitals and also because of travelling to the hospital and hospital.

Therefore it appears that,
the delay in filing FIR is properly explained.

24. The Counsel for the Respondent No.1 argued that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner and denied about involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident.
The respondent No.3 has contended that Ex.R.1 has been tampered and over written as 'RTA' in the place of 'assault'.
The author of Ex.R.1 has been examined as RW.1 in her evidence, she Gangadhar.

6 has clearly stated that, the patient was brought in the mid-night 12.40 a.m. with bleeding, she was writing as well as treating the patient by mistake assault was written.
RW.1 has specifically stated that, by mistake it was mentioned as assault same sentence is continued as by Bolero near Gopalan Mall.
On perusal of Ex.R.1, it appears that, it has been written continuously as a "history of assault by Bolero near Gopalan Mall".
Later, the word 'assault' has been scratched and 'RTA' is written.
While writing the sentence only the word assault has been written but, other things as by Bolero is written.
Therefore, it appears that the word 'assault' has been wrongly written and it has been corrected later.
The contention of the counsel for respondent No.3 that, the word 'RTA' has been over written to help the petitioner holds no water.

25. On perusal of Ex.P.2 complaint, Ex.P.3 the spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 sketch and Ex.P.9 charge sheet,
it appears that, the accident occurred at opposite of the Gopalan Mall Bengaluru, as the driver of the driver of Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51/B-9206 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle from back side and caused the accident.

Further,
RW.2 the I.O. has clearly stated that, he has secured the CC TV footage's and vehicle number from the Toll and traced the vehicle.
On perusal of Ex.P.5 the IMV report, it appears that the offending vehicle was sustained front right side bumper dent and scratched.
So it clearly indicates that the offending vehicle involved in the accident.

Further on perusal of charge sheet it discloses that, the Jeevan Bhima Nagar Police have filed the case against the driver of Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51/B-9206 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and U/Sec.134(a)(b)
r/w Sec.187 of IMV Act.
The said charge sheet has not been challenged by the owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, it appears that, the said accident is caused by the offending Bolero Vehicle.
Further, there is no any material to hold that, there is a contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.

26. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.

27. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P.1-F.I.R. Ex.P.2-first information, Ex.P.3-spot mahazar,
Ex.P.4-Sketch, Ex.P.5- IMV report, Ex.P.6-Wound certificate and Ex.P.9-Charge sheet, it appears that, as on the date of alleged accident, the driver of offending vehicle drove his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, came at high speed and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.

Therefore considering all these aspects, this Tribunal come to conclusion that, the said accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51/B-9206.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
28. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner claimed the compensation amount of Rs.75,00,000/-.

As per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, the petitioner had sustained following injuries:-
1) Cut lacerated wound to the occipital region sutures done.
Gangadhar.M vs Syed Vahid on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161400527/
7

The doctor opined that, the said injury is grievous in nature and patient condition at high risk,
admitted in ICU.

Hence, by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioner is entitled for amount of Rs.50,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
29. The petitioner had produced 40 medical bills and 19 medical prescription which are marked as Ex.P.14 and Ex.P.15.
The said bills have not been denied by the respondents.
There is no any contradiction to disbelieve the said bills.
Hence, by considering the bills, the petitioner is entitled to claim the amount of Rs.73,068/- under the head of medical expenditure.
30. As per Ex.P.10 and 11 discharge summaries the petitioner took treatment at NIMHANS Hospital from 24.04.2022 and 25.04.2022 and also from 10-05-2022 to 31-05-2022 total for 24 days.
Therefore, by considering the period of treatment taken as inpatient this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.24,000/- under the head Transportation, Nourishment and Conveyance charges.
31. To prove the disability, neither the petitioner had examined his treated doctor to prove the disability, nor produced any disability certificate.
Hence the petitioner is not entitled to claim any compensation amount under the head loss of income on account of permanent disability and also under the head of the future medical expenses.

However by considering the period of treatment taken as inpatient and as per Ex.P.6 wound certificate the petitioner sustained grievous injury, this tribunal award reasonable compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
32. The petitioner sustained injuries and also took treatment as an inpatient.
Therefore considering the nature of injuries this Tribunal has award the amount of Rs.30,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of amenities.

33. Considering oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:

34. Interest:

For awarding interest, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest can be awarded in MVC Cases, cannot be more than 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Hence, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
35. Liability:-
As per the Petition, the Respondent No.1 to 3 are the RC Owner, insured & Insurer of the Bolero Maxi Truck bearing Reg.No.KA-51/B-9206.

As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, hence Respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Further the Respondent No.3 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 in the Partly Affirmative.

36. Issue No.3: For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.2,07,068/- interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 to 3 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Further, Respondent No.3 being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, the entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner with proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
JUDGMENT The Petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 against respondents, for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
5. This accident occurred due to negligence of the driver of the Bolero Maxi Truck bearing Reg.No.KA-51/B-9206, hence, the Jeevan Bhimanagar Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of said vehicle in crime No.36/2022 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 to 3 are owner and insurers of the vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prayed to grant the compensation.
Respondent No.2 did not appear before the Tribunal and hence he was placed exparte.
7.
On the fault of the petitioner the accident had occurred and due to his negligence he has touched the back side of the vehicle.
Further, respondent No.1 has denied the name, address, age, income and occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by him and disability caused to him and also contended that, claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
The Bolero Maxi Truck not at all dashed to the motorcycle, but to get compensation the petitioner files a false case against the driver of the Bolero Maxi Truck bearing Reg.No.KA-51/B-9206.
The petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties such as owner and insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41/H-4902 and also denied the issuance of insurance policy for the Bolero Maxi Truck vehicle.
opennyai_summary.issue:
9. On basis of the Pleadings and materials, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 20.04.2022 at about 11.30 p.m the petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41/H-4902 proceeding on Old Madras Road from NGRF towards K.R. Puram, when he reached near opposite Gopalan Mall at that time driver of one Bolero Maxi Truck bearing Reg.No.KA-51/B-9206, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering human life, came at high speed and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to forced impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous Injuries on vital parts of the body?
2)Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
3) Whether order or award?
10.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The petitioner filed this petition against the respondents for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
Gangadhar.M vs Syed Vahid on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161400527/
So it clearly indicates that the offending vehicle involved in the accident.
Further on perusal of charge sheet it discloses that, the Jeevan Bhima Nagar Police have filed the case against the driver of Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51/B-9206 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and U/Sec.134(a)(b)
r/w Sec.187 of IMV Act.
The said charge sheet has not been challenged by the owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, it appears that, the said accident is caused by the offending Bolero Vehicle.
Further, there is no any material to hold that, there is a contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.
26. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.
The petitioner claimed the compensation amount of Rs.75,00,000/-.
Hence, by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioner is entitled for amount of Rs.50,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
The said bills have not been denied by the respondents.
There is no any contradiction to disbelieve the said bills.
Therefore, by considering the period of treatment taken as inpatient this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.24,000/- under the head Transportation, Nourishment and Conveyance charges.
Hence the petitioner is not entitled to claim any compensation amount under the head loss of income on account of permanent disability and also under the head of the future medical expenses.
For awarding interest, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest can be awarded in MVC Cases, cannot be more than 6% p.a.
opennyai_summary.arguments: 20. The Counsel for the petitioner argued that, the 2 days delay in filing of the complaint has been properly explained as injured was in Coma, in Ex.P.19 the history is clearly mentioned as hit by bolero truck.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, by considering the bills, the petitioner is entitled to claim the amount of Rs.73,068/- under the head of medical expenditure.
However by considering the period of treatment taken as inpatient and as per Ex.P.6 wound certificate the petitioner sustained grievous injury, this tribunal award reasonable compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
Therefore considering the nature of injuries this Tribunal has award the amount of Rs.30,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of amenities.
33. Considering oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:
Sl.
 Under the Heads Amount in Rs.
 No.
 1. Pain and sufferings 50,000-00  2. Medical expenses, 73,068-00
charges
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,07,068/-.
Hence, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
35. Liability:-
As per the Petition, the Respondent No.1 to 3 are the RC Owner, insured & Insurer of the Bolero Maxi Truck bearing Reg.No.KA-51/B-9206.
As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, hence Respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Further the Respondent No.3 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 in the Partly Affirmative.
36. Issue No.3: For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.2,07,068/- interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 to 3 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Further, Respondent No.3 being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, the entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner with proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
